title: Phoenix R4 Deletion Research Summary

final_method.name: R4-4D2B TARGET-normalized CTC hypothesis scoring
final_method.acoustic_model: self-trained CNN plus one-layer bidirectional GRU CTC phone-sequence model
final_method.threshold_source: ordinary float64 median of 12 TRAIN-speaker LOSO fold thresholds
final_method.decision: D_i >= theta predicts deletion; otherwise KEEP versus BEST_SUB predicts correct or substitution

positive_findings: CNN plus BiGRU CTC substantially improved phone-sequence acoustic modeling versus CNN-only CTC.
CTC hypothesis scoring strongly reduced greedy false deletions.
Deletion-versus-substitution continuous discrimination was meaningfully above chance.
Speaker-held-out TARGET normalization and calibration improved robustness relative to the original RAW threshold.
The final TARGET validation nevertheless failed the frozen confirmation requirements.
interpretation: The frozen BiGRU CTC model produced useful continuous deletion-related acoustic evidence, but the resulting decision layer did not achieve the required validation precision/recall/F1 and matched-control gates.
capstone_ready_conclusion: Phoenix demonstrated measurable acoustic evidence for pronunciation deletion through a self-trained CNN+BiGRU CTC sequence model and CTC hypothesis scoring. However, the final frozen validation protocol did not meet the predefined deletion confirmation criteria. Therefore deletion detection is retained as a current research limitation and was not evaluated on the untouched final R4 TEST split.
separation_from_other_findings: Phoenix findings for correct and substitution remain separate from the unconfirmed deletion branch.
